key_insight: The paper shows that nonlinear dynamics can be embedded into fully coherent, ancilla-free quantum circuits, with query cost determined by how sensitive the dynamics are to initial conditions.
engineering_relevance: This provides a route to resource-efficient quantum simulation of nonlinear systems by linking algorithm design to dynamical stability, helping estimate when coherent embeddings are feasible and optimal.
method: Generalize the ancilla-free double-bracket algorithm by replacing the state-independent Hamiltonian with a state-dependent Hermitian operator.
Recursively call an initial-state preparation oracle and its inverse to build a fully coherent, ancilla-free unitary embedding.
Classify query complexity by dynamical behavior: contractive, nonexpansive, or expansive.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports query upper bounds of exp(O(T)), exp(O(T^2)), and exp(exp(O(T))) for the three dynamical regimes, and an optimal worst-case complexity Theta(e^{gT/2}) for the discrete Gross--Pitaevskii equation.
watch_item: The approach is asymptotic and oracle-based, so practical performance will depend on the cost and stability of state-preparation oracles and on how accurately the nonlinear model can be encoded.
paper_title: Quantum Complexity of Ancilla-Free Unitary Embeddings for Nonlinear Dynamics via Generalized State-Dependent Double-Bracket Flows
